q: Do clinical (human wound/bacteremia), aquaculture (catfish/tilapia/carp outbreak), and environmental (water/sediment) Aeromonas veronii isolates form clean, non-overlapping pathotype clades on gene-repertoire — or is the ML09-123↔TH0426 aquaculture clone the exception rather than the rule?
basis: Section 4.1 of REPORT.md shows ML09-123 and TH0426 are essentially clonal (fastANI 99.927%, mash d=0.00171, VFDB Jaccard 1.000) and 3.4% ANI-separated from the next-nearest strain — this is one clade of two, not a species-wide pathotype survey. The paper compared 41 genomes across human, cattle, fish, water, and sediment sources across 9 countries; the replication reproduces the ML/TH clade but does not test whether host-of-isolation is generally predictive of gene content across the other 39 genomes (or, more importantly, across the ~1,927 A. veronii genomes NCBI now holds, a 47× expansion since the 2018 cutoff noted in §3.1).
next_steps: (1) Pull all ~1,927 current NCBI A. veronii assemblies via NCBI Datasets v2; (2) mine BioSample host + isolation-source fields (regex-normalize free-text 'catfish/channel catfish/Ictalurus/tilapia/carp/pond water/human blood/wound' etc.); (3) cluster genomes by VFDB profile (Jaccard) and by mash distance; (4) test with a permutation ANOVA whether host category is a significant predictor of cluster membership, controlling for country and year; (5) specifically ask whether the ML09-123/TH0426 clone-clade has expanded — how many post-2018 genomes fall inside it and where geographically.

q: For the variable virulence clusters (T3SS in 31/41, T6SS in 28/41, TAD in 12/41), are those loci chromosomally integrated in genomic islands or plasmid-borne — i.e. is the pathotype variability driven by vertical loss or by ongoing horizontal transfer?
basis: Section 4.4 of REPORT.md establishes that T3SS/T6SS/TAD are variably present across the 41 genomes but the replication used VFDB gene presence only — it never asked WHERE (chromosome vs plasmid vs integrated genomic island) those loci sit. Section 8 explicitly lists 'plasmid vs chromosomal location of the variable T3SS/T6SS/TAD loci' as un-tested. Without that, we cannot distinguish 'ancestrally present, sometimes lost' from 'occasionally horizontally acquired' — and those two scenarios have very different one-health implications.
next_steps: (1) For the 41 assemblies, extract circular replicons vs contigs > mash-classify each contig against a plasmid reference set (PLSDB / MOB-suite); (2) for draft assemblies, run PlasFlow or platon to predict plasmid vs chromosomal origin per contig; (3) locate the VFDB T3SS/T6SS/TAD hits on classified contigs and tally chromosome vs plasmid per system; (4) run IslandViewer/mobileOG-db on the ML09-123 chromosome to test whether these clusters sit inside canonical genomic islands with recognizable integrase + tRNA insertion signatures; (5) if plasmid-borne, BLAST the flanking mobilization genes against Aeromonas + Enterobacteriaceae plasmid backbones to trace horizontal-transfer origin.

q: Does the classical A. veronii bv. veronii vs bv. sobria (ornithine-decarboxylase-positive vs -negative biovar) subspecies split hold up as a clean phylogenomic dichotomy, or is it a paraphyletic artifact of one biochemical test?
basis: REPORT.md (§4.2) confirms species coherence — all 1,640 non-self fastANI pairs fall in [95.9%, 100.0%] — but does not touch the historical bv. veronii vs bv. sobria distinction, and the paper (§1 summary in REPORT.md) treats the 41 as one species set without stratifying by biovar. The replication's mash dendrogram (Fig. phylo_dendrogram.png) exists but the report never reads out whether biovar labels segregate on it.
next_steps: (1) Manually curate biovar (veronii/sobria/'unknown') for as many of the 41 strains as NCBI BioSample + literature permits; (2) overlay biovar labels onto the mash dendrogram and the fastANI heatmap; (3) test monophyly of each biovar with a proper core-genome ML tree (IQ-TREE on a Roary/Panaroo core alignment, 1000 UFBoot replicates); (4) if biovar is polyphyletic, test whether presence/absence of the ornithine-decarboxylase gene (speC/speF orthologs) actually tracks the biochemical call — i.e. is the biovar assignment even genetically consistent within a strain?

q: Does the diversity and copy number of quorum-sensing regulators (luxR/luxI family, AhyR/AhyI in Aeromonas) correlate with pathotype — i.e. do aquaculture-outbreak strains carry a distinctive QS regulator complement vs environmental strains?
basis: REPORT.md §4.5 reports 159 distinct VFDB genes across 41 genomes with 101 (63.5%) being variable/accessory and a per-genome VF-load range of 66-140 — but the replication never breaks the accessory pool down by functional category. Quorum-sensing regulators are exactly the kind of virulence-adjacent gene where copy-number and paralog diversity plausibly track host-adaptation, and neither the paper's VFDB-setB screen (as summarized in REPORT.md) nor this replication's abricate/VFDB screen reports QS-regulator counts separately.
next_steps: (1) From the 41 protein FASTAs already downloaded (§3.1), HMMER-search against Pfam/TIGRFAM profiles for LuxR (PF00196), LuxI/autoinducer-synthetase (PF00765), and the Aeromonas-specific AhyR/AhyI orthologs; (2) tabulate per-genome QS-regulator counts and paralog diversity; (3) correlate against host-of-isolation category (from Q1) and against clinical-outbreak vs asymptomatic-carrier metadata; (4) specifically test whether the ML09-123/TH0426 clone carries a QS complement that is unusual for the species or is just the species mode.

q: How prevalent is MDR / plasmid-borne AMR carriage among aquaculture A. veronii isolates, and — via mobilizable plasmid backbones shared with Enterobacteriaceae — what is the plausible one-health transfer risk to human populations that eat farmed fish?
basis: REPORT.md §8 explicitly lists 'MDR / AMR carriage' among the un-tested questions in the replication. The paper focused on virulence-factor comparative genomics via VFDB and did not report a CARD/ResFinder AMR screen (as summarized in REPORT.md's paper summary). Given the ML09-123↔TH0426 clone spans US and Chinese aquaculture, the transfer-risk question is directly downstream of the paper's own 'globally disseminated pathotype' framing but is not addressed by either the paper or the replication.
next_steps: (1) Run abricate against CARD, ResFinder, ARG-ANNOT, MEGARes, and PlasmidFinder on the same 41 assemblies (tools are already installed per §3.6); (2) tally per-genome AMR-gene counts and drug-class coverage; (3) cross-reference AMR hits with the plasmid classification from Q2 to identify plasmid-borne AMR; (4) BLAST the plasmid backbones carrying AMR against a curated Enterobacteriaceae plasmid set (IncF, IncH, IncI, IncX) to test whether these backbones are compatible with transfer to human enteric pathogens; (5) expand to the current ~1,927 NCBI A. veronii genomes and stratify AMR/MDR rates by isolation source (aquaculture vs clinical vs environmental) and by country to test whether aquaculture is over-represented among MDR-carrier strains.
